extracted.intended_audience: general public, policymakers, platform operators, researchers interested in disinformation policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the EU Code of Practice on Disinformation: the Code's working definition of disinformation and the commitments industry signatories agree to adopt to address online disinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disinformation is defined as 'verifiably false or misleading information which, cumulatively, (a) Is created, presented and disseminated for economic gain or to intentionally deceive the public; and (b) May cause public harm, intended as threats to democratic political and policymaking processes as well as public goods such as the protection of EU citizens' health, the environment or security.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Code's working definition used to identify content covered by commitments. It highlights both intent/economic motive and potential to cause public harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions to the definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code recognizes that the definition excludes 'misleading advertising, reporting errors, satire and parody, or clearly identified partisan news and commentary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are explicitly carved out so that normal journalistic mistakes, clearly labelled satire, and overt partisan commentary are not treated as disinformation under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutiny of advertisement placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories acknowledge the need to 'significantly improve the scrutiny of advertisement placements, notably in order to reduce revenues of the purveyors of disinformation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This commitment focuses on reducing the economic incentives for purveyors of disinformation by changing ad-placement practices and advertiser controls. Implementation examples would include vetting ad placements and preventing monetization of disinformation sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency for political and issue-based advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories 'acknowledge the [European Commission's] call to recognise the importance of ensuring transparency about political and issue-based advertising.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires measures to disclose who is funding political/issue ads and make targeting/transparency information available to the public and regulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of services (fake accounts and bots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories recognize 'the importance of intensifying and demonstrating the effectiveness of efforts to close fake accounts as well as the importance of establishing clear marking systems and rules for bots to ensure their activities cannot be confused with human interactions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers account quality, detection/removal of inauthentic accounts, and clear labelling/behaviour rules for automated actors (bots) so platform interactions are not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowering consumers (ranking and prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories commit to 'invest in technological means to prioritize relevant, authentic, and authoritative information where appropriate in search, feeds, or other automatically ranked distribution channels.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This focuses on algorithmic and product changes to surface higher-quality information and demote likely disinformation in ranking, recommendations, or search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empowering the research community
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories 'commit to support good faith independent efforts to track disinformation and understand its impact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes commitments to provide researchers with access, tools, or data (consistent with privacy law) to study disinformation, its spread, and effects, enabling independent evaluation of platforms' practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual self-assessment reports for Commission review
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories commit to prepare annual self-assessment reports for review by the European Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural accountability mechanism: platforms must report annually on implementation of the Code so the Commission (and public) can assess compliance and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible uptake / selective adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code 'sets out five broad commitments for industry signatories and allows for flexible uptake. Signatories may select which commitments they will adhere to depending on the nature of their services and their technical capabilities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code is voluntary and adaptable: signatories are not required to adopt all commitments identically; implementation is intended to be proportionate to each signatory's service model and capabilities.
